solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Before a crustacean swallowed head of stag beetle

indicators.note: placed first in the clue, it says the letter from the deer comes ahead of the rest
the head of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of stag

indicators.note: whatever is swallowed ends up inside the swallower, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a crab is a crustacean
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crab gobbles up part of a stag, which is a strange meal for any shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: The crab swallows the A, giving C-A-RAB, and the S from stag goes in front: SCARAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarab is a dung beetle, sacred in ancient Egypt and common as a carved amulet.

clue.text: Illustration shows batting position

parts.note: a batter at the crease in cricket is said to be in
a stance is a position taken up

explanation.surface: A coaching manual's picture demonstrates how to stand at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batting position' reads as one cricket phrase, but it splits in two; a batter at the crease in cricket is said to be in.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is an example, and an illustration is an example given to make a point clear.

clue.text: Perhaps mouse is unimportant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a device plugged into a computer, of which a mouse is one example
second meaning: on the margins, not central

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a mouse as a creature of no consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouse' suggests the rodent; here it is the computer accessory, an example of a device attached to a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for an add-on computer device and an adjective for something marginal or minor.

clue.text: Continent is up for replacing inhabitants of Africa

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top
one thing standing in for another means the clue's inner letters are swapped out

parts.note: taken as written
the inhabitants of a word are its inner letters, all but the first and last

explanation.surface: A note that one continent's peoples are being displaced by another's.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of the word Africa stay put; only its middle is swapped for the turned-round word.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest of the continents, stretching from the Urals to the Pacific.

clue.text: Surface tension just absorbed by oxygen

indicators.note: by can mean beside, so the oxygen symbol is set next to the rest

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken right inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: just in the sense of reasonable or sound
T is the physics symbol for tension

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: surface tension is simply taken up by oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surface tension' looks like one physics term, but 'Surface' is the definition. T goes inside SENSIBLE (S-T-ENSIBLE), with O beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensible means apparent on the face of things, so it describes what is only surface-deep.

clue.text: Punter places this to help

definitions.note: a two-word phrase, A BET, run together
definitions.meaning: first meaning: what a gambler puts on a horse, split as two words
second meaning: to assist, usually in wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A gambler puts money on a horse to give it a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: A punter is a gambler; what they place is A BET, which run together gives ABET.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist or encourage, chiefly in a crime, as in aiding and abetting.

clue.text: Beer's picked up for pound

indicators.note: picking something up by ear means hearing it, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: beer is a brew, so beer is becomes brew's, said brews

explanation.surface: A pub-goer notices that a pint has been bought for a pound coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' tempts as money, but it is a verb meaning to batter.
explanation.definitionFit: To bruise is to crush or injure by beating, and to pound food or flesh does exactly that.

clue.text: Use this for playing musical on TV

parts.note: Chess is a 1980s stage musical by Tim Rice and the men of ABBA
a TV is a television set

explanation.surface: Advice to use a television for watching a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing musical' looks like a phrase, but the definition stops at 'playing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess set is the board and pieces you need in order to play a game of chess.

clue.text: Agreement for government survey about official organisation

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a census is an official count of the population
the ONS is Britain's Office for National Statistics, which runs the census

explanation.surface: Agreement is needed for a state survey of a public body.
explanation.walkthrough: The Office for National Statistics is the UK body that actually conducts the census, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A consensus is general agreement shared by a whole group.

clue.text: Slip caught this delivery

parts.note: surface reading: a cricket fielder in the slips takes a catch off a ball bowled
setter's reading: a baby slips out and is caught by the midwife, and the event is a delivery

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the slips stand beside the wicketkeeper and a delivery is a bowled ball; here a delivery is a baby arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: A delivery in a maternity ward is the moment a child is born.

clue.text: One detects light capturing surface of sparkling wine

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor

parts.note: the retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye

indicators.note: the surface of a word is its top layer, so just its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of sparkling

explanation.surface: Someone holds a glass of fizz up to the light and spots the bubbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sparkling wine' reads as one phrase, but 'sparkling' only lends its first letter; retsina is not fizzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Demands guts to give up resistance

indicators.note: giving something up means losing it, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: entrails are the guts of an animal
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Someone insists that cowardice means abandoning the fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guts' suggests courage, but it means innards; ENTRAILS without its R leaves ENTAILS.
explanation.definitionFit: If one thing entails another, it necessarily requires or involves it.

clue.text: Censor incomplete report

indicators.note: something incomplete is missing its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a report is the sound of a gunshot, a bang

explanation.surface: A censor suppresses a report that was never finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' looks like a document to be censored, but it is the noise of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To censor is to suppress or prohibit, which is what a ban does.

clue.text: Not Mr. Homer Simpson — a different man

indicators.note: a different arrangement means the remaining letters are reordered
not means without, so the title's letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
the title, without its full stop
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cartoon dad is declared to be a different kind of man altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M and R from HOMER SIMPSON, add A, and rearrange the eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Homo sapiens is the scientific name for the human species, mankind.

clue.text: Short of gold, mountaineers brewed soup

indicators.note: brewing mixes and stews ingredients, so the letters are stirred into a new order
being short of something means lacking it, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
taken as written

explanation.surface: Climbers who can't afford better cook up soup at camp.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A and U out of MOUNTAINEERS and rearrange the ten letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Minestrone is a thick Italian vegetable soup, often with pasta or rice.

clue.text: Old man more unwell after getting tattoo — needs this?

definitions.text: Old man more unwell after getting tattoo — needs this?

indicators.note: after says the sickly piece follows the body-art piece in the line

parts.note: pa is a father, an old man
a tattoo is informally called ink
comparative of ill

explanation.surface: A father feels worse after his first tattoo and wants something for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: PA, then INK, then ILLER.
explanation.definitionFit: An analgesic is what an elderly man in pain after a tattoo session would reach for.

clue.text: Clip art detailed by that woman

indicators.note: de-tailed means having its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: she is the pronoun for that woman
taken as written

explanation.surface: Clip art finished in fine detail by a female designer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' reads as intricate but splits as de-tailed: ART loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: To shear is to clip or cut, as with sheep's wool or a hedge.

clue.text: Symptoms initially given impression of agitation

indicators.note: initially points to the start of the word, so only its opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of symptoms
an impression is a print run of a book, an edition

explanation.surface: A doctor notes that the early symptoms suggest a nervous condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agitation' sounds medical, but here it means stirring up unrest against the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedition is political agitation or incitement to rebel against authority.

clue.text: Pinch of salt at noon

parts.note: N is short for noon
a salt is a sailor, an able-bodied seaman or AB

explanation.surface: Adding a pinch of salt to lunch at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinch of salt' reads as a kitchen measure, but 'Pinch' is the definition and 'salt' a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinch and nab are both slang for steal or arrest.

clue.text: Block chain reduced by more than half with energy and time

indicators.note: cut down by over half means most of the word's letters are thrown away

parts.note: taken as written
go means energy or drive
T is short for time

explanation.surface: A blockchain is cut down to size with power and patience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Block chain' reads as the crypto ledger, but 'Block' is the definition. CHAIN loses three of its five letters, leaving IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block of cast metal, such as a gold bar.

clue.text: Psychologically coerce Georgia with insult

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
a slight is an insult or snub

explanation.surface: Bullying a whole country into submission through slurs.
explanation.definitionFit: To gaslight someone is to manipulate them into doubting their own perception, after the film Gaslight.

clue.text: Misinformation regarding climax of tennis match?

parts.note: doubles is a tennis match with two players a side
a peak is a climax or high point

explanation.surface: Fake news about the decisive point of a tennis final.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical split: the high point of a doubles match is a doubles peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Doublespeak is deliberately evasive or misleading language, Orwell-style.

clue.text: Blurb an editor abridged and refined

indicators.note: an abridged text is cut at both ends, so the letters left in the middle make the word

parts.note: the run of letters inside these words

explanation.surface: A book's blurb is cut down and polished by its editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Urbane means suave and courteous, with polished city manners.

clue.text: Problem wrestling with lost love

indicators.note: with something lost means minus it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: sumo is Japanese wrestling
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone is struggling with a lost romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrestling with' reads as struggling with, but wrestling is a sport here.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is an arithmetic problem, as in a schoolchild doing sums.

clue.text: Cross repeatedly assuming Gandalf to begin with is not a wizard

indicators.note: assuming means taking on or taking in, so the letters go inside

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey

indicators.note: to begin with means at the start, so just the opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of Gandalf

indicators.note: repeatedly says the selected letter is used more than once, here twice

parts.note: the same letter again, as the clue asks for it more than once

explanation.surface: Gandalf crossing a wizard's path, fitting for Tolkien's wizard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb but is the hybrid animal; MULE takes in G twice: MU-GG-LE.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Harry Potter books a Muggle is a person with no magical powers.

clue.text: Blank slate lacking as a format for spreadsheets

definitions.note: a noun phrase for an adjective: tabular data is in that format

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the following letters are taken away

parts.note: tabula rasa is Latin for a blank slate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A blank spreadsheet is said to lack something as a format.
explanation.walkthrough: TABULA RASA minus its final A-S-A leaves TABULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabular means arranged in rows and columns, which is exactly how spreadsheets lay out data.

clue.text: Song was flat?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a German art song, as by Schubert

definitions.note: playful: lied as told an untruth, read as lay flat
definitions.meaning: second meaning: past tense of lie, reclining, used loosely

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' suggests a singer off pitch; the second sense is lying down, with a wink that LIED is properly the past of telling fibs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lied is a German art song for voice and piano; lied is also a past form of lie.

clue.text: Hearty meal should be what dentist gives you

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the material that plugs a cavity in a tooth

explanation.surface: A big lunch ought to be what you get at the dentist's.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for food that satisfies hunger and a noun for a dental repair.

clue.text: Vampire has more than one lover with unforgiving heart

parts.note: a fan is a lover or enthusiast

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letter is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of this eleven-letter word

explanation.surface: A vampire juggles several lovers and shows no mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More than one lover' tempts as the wordplay, but 'more than one' belongs to the definition: a vampire has two of these.
explanation.definitionFit: A fang is a long pointed tooth, and the stock vampire has a pair.

clue.text: "Once upon…" at the beginning carried little weight

indicators.note: what is carried is held within the carrier

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which is all that is used

parts.note: the first letter of upon

explanation.surface: The opening of a fairy tale had little impact on its listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: ONCE holds the U from upon after its first letter: O-U-NCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a small unit of weight, about 28 grams.

clue.text: Lanthanide ethanol mixture won't kill you

indicators.note: a mixture has its parts stirred together, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Ln is the general chemical symbol for any lanthanide element
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemist reassures us that a lab mixture is harmless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lanthanide' tempts as fodder in full, but it gives only its group symbol Ln.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nonlethal is not deadly, so it will not cause death.
